messages:
olivia: Heads up 914 folks — a customer copy/pasted our Go quickstart into an HTTP handler and saw generator goroutine growth. The snippet used context.Background() when creating the stream.

samir: Yeah that pattern shows up a lot. Quickstart should demonstrate using the request context (r.Context()) or a derived timeout. Also show defer gen.Close() right after creation.

hana: Example we can use in docs: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 15*time.Second)
defer cancel()
gen := client.Generator(ctx, req)
defer gen.Close()
for gen.Next() { /* handle tokens */ }
```
Keep client long-lived but pass ctx into calls.

olivia: Another bug: our retry helper sleeps for backoff with time.Sleep, so if ctx is canceled the sleep doesn't abort and goroutines stick around. I filed #3598 with a repro.

pete: I pushed a tiny change to the retry util: use time.NewTimer and select on timer.C and ctx.Done() so backoffs are abortable. Added a unit test that cancels ctx and ensures the retry returns early.

samir: Can we add a smoke test for the generator stream: start stream, cancel ctx, wait short window, assert goroutine count returns to baseline? That would catch regressions in CI.

hana: Agreed. Also note API parity: generator exposes Close(), but other streams sometimes use CloseStream(). We should standardize the name; created RFC issue to discuss.

devops-bot: CI: build 7743 on branch fix/go-gen-retry-cancel 6809 passed :white_check_mark:

olivia: Great. Action items: docs PR to patch quickstart and call out "do not use context.Background() for request-scoped streams", merge retry fix, add generator leak test, and track API parity RFC. I'll assign reviewers.

samir: Thanks all 44d will watch the deploy and update the sample-app repro.
